questions.question: Which is NOT a good way for a rider to increase visibility?
questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers
questions.explanation: To be visible to other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: When another vehicle is following too closely, you should:

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. Change lanes and let them pass when it is safe. Speeding up only increases danger by encouraging higher-speed tailgating.

questions.question: To increase visibility, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Approved helmets:

options.text: Can limit the view of the rider.
Allow the rider to see far to the sides as needed.
Do not have to be worn if the rider thinks their view would be limited.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the rider to see far to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not limit your vision. Any approved helmet lets you see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: How reflective your tires are
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tread depth, and the condition of your tire sidewalls and tread surface.

questions.question: Drivers on an entrance ramp may not see you. How can you help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane—it is not your responsibility.
Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
Weave within your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if it is safe to do so. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to create space for the merging driver.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You can finish the pass in a no passing zone.
You may go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You must complete the pass on the shoulder if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: Passing must be done within the posted speed limit and only in areas where passing is legal and safe.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting your motorcycle, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work properly. Clean the mirrors and make sure the fuel supply valve is open.

questions.question: When someone follows you too closely, you should:

options.text: Focus on the road in front and ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only increases danger. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers do not expect you there.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding at night, how fast should you go?

options.text: Slower than you would during the day.
The same speed as you would during the day.
Faster than you would during the day.
On the shoulder so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than during the day. It is hard to see hazards in the dark. Slowing down helps you avoid accidents.

questions.question: When hitting a bump or pothole, why should you rise slightly off your seat?

options.text: So you can jump off if you need to.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb the impact. This reduces the force that hits you and keeps you on the motorcycle.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips under five miles long at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: What is a major effect of alcohol on your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your body functions slow down.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down your physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help you avoid a crash?

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on hoping others see you. Make yourself visible, signal your plans clearly, keep space between you and other vehicles, and watch for hazards ahead.

questions.question: What should you remember when going through a curve?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Always stay on the left side of the lane.
Always stay on the right side of the lane.
The best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions change. Be ready to move your position in the lane. The best path through a curve does not always match the road's curve.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders sit in a group?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: New riders should ride just behind the leader. This puts them near the front so experienced riders behind them can watch them.

questions.question: What group formation is best for curves, turns, and highway entrances?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation through curves, turns, and when entering or leaving highways. Use staggered formation on straight roads.

questions.question: How can you stop other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Give dirty looks if someone enters your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in beside you.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle weaves on rain grooves or bridge gratings?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip tightly and speed up to get past it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving on grooves and gratings is not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT reduce your chances of having an accident?

options.text: Spotting hazards and deciding which ones to handle first.
Keeping space between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide which to handle first. Always use your headlight so others can see you. Keep space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: When you make a normal stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze the front brake hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This habit helps you stop quickly if needed. Practice using both brakes during normal stops.

questions.question: Good motorcyclists know they are safest when:

options.text: They go faster than other vehicles.
They ride on the edge of the road.
They stay on the left side of their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers can see them.
questions.explanation: Good riders are safest when other drivers can see them clearly. Use your headlight, brake light, turn signals, and correct lane position to stay visible.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT protect you in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose thick, durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Is only dangerous if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops you from steering.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is very dangerous and can cause a serious crash. When you brake too hard, the rear wheel locks and you lose the ability to steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: When using a sidecar to carry something, you should:

options.text: Tie down the load so it does not shift.
Place the load loose in the seat.
Tie the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tie down the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure your load so it cannot move and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place the load toward the back of the sidecar to prevent the sidecar from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is usually located near the right footrest.

questions.question: When you adjust your mirrors, you should be able to see:

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. A small part of your arm or shoulder may show, but seeing the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of the braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of the braking power.
Should only be used when the road is wet.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of the braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of your total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.
